assumptions: Daily demand will revert to the baseline forecast of 50 units/day after promotion PROMO-1 ends on 2026-09-23.
args.rationale:
Investigation of the demand spike trigger indicates that recent daily sales of 130 units/day (2.6x forecast) are driven by active promotion PROMO-1 ('Spike promo'), running from 2026-09-07 to 2026-09-23. Guidance specifies that promotional uplift ends with the promotion and should not be extrapolated. Extrapolating this elevated demand across the 28-day horizon (Candidate 3: 3,550 units) is infeasible due to breaching the max days cover policy (63 days vs 12-day limit).

Under baseline demand (50 units/day over 28 days = 1,400 total units demand), the current usable inventory of 1,000 units drops below the 200-unit safety stock threshold on 2026-10-03 and stocks out on 2026-10-07, creating 400 unmet units.

Placing a purchase order with SUP-A for 600 units at $14.00/unit (total $8,400.00) with a 7-day lead time yields delivery on 2026-09-24. Simulation confirms this plan is feasible, reduces total unmet demand from 400 to 0 units, maintains closing inventory at 200 units (4.0 days of cover, well within the 12-day limit), and respects physical storage constraints (45 m³ peak occupancy vs 200 m³ headroom).

Because the total purchase cost of $8,400.00 exceeds the buyer autonomy spend limit of $2,000.00 (though within the $50,000.00 total available budget), this plan requires buyer approval.
important_factors: Recent sales spike of 130 units/day is driven by PROMO-1, which ends on 2026-09-23 and must not be extrapolated across the planning horizon.
Baseline demand of 50 units/day yields a 28-day horizon demand of 1,400 units against 1,000 units usable on-hand inventory.
Without action, stockout occurs on 2026-10-07 resulting in 400 unmet units and 12 days below safety stock (200 units).
Ordering 600 units from SUP-A for receipt on 2026-09-24 eliminates all 400 unmet units and leaves closing inventory at the 200-unit safety stock level.
Extrapolating the sales spike (Candidate 3, 3,550 units) is infeasible as it results in 63 days of cover, breaching the 12-day max cover policy limit.
Total order cost of $8,400.00 is within the available budget of $50,000.00 but exceeds the $2,000.00 autonomy spend limit, requiring buyer approval.
